code: fit$jags_code ## model { ##   # mcp helper values ##   cp_0 = CONST1_ ##   cp_2 = CONST2_ ##  ##   # Priors for population-level effects ##   cp_1 ~ dunif(CONST1_, CONST2_)  # Within the observed change-point span ##   cp_1_sd ~ dnorm(0, 1/(197.7306)^2) T(0,)  # Group-level change-point variation ##   Intercept_1 ~ dt(22.5, 1/(5.8)^2, 3)   # Robustly centered mean intercept with a minimum scale of 2.5 ##   x_2 ~ dt(0, 1/(0.1173314)^2, 3)   # Regularizing mean coefficient scaled to a reference predictor change ##   sigma_1 ~ dt(0, 1/(5.8)^2, 3) T(0,)  # Positive residual SD calibrated on the response scale ##  ##   # Priors for varying effects ##   for (id_ in 1:n_unique_id) { ##     cp_1_id_uncentered[id_] ~ dnorm(CONST3_, 1/(cp_1_sd)^2) T(CONST1_-cp_1,CONST2_-cp_1)  # Zero-centered group-level change-point offsets ##   } ##   cp_1_id = cp_1_id_uncentered - mean(cp_1_id_uncentered)  # vectorized zero-centering ##  ##   # Model and likelihood ##   for (i_ in 1:length(x)) { ##     # par_x local to each segment ##     x_local_1_[i_] = min(x[i_], (cp_1 + cp_1_id[id[i_]])) ##     x_local_2_[i_] = min(x[i_], cp_2) - (cp_1 + cp_1_id[id[i_]]) ##      ##     # Formula for mu ##     link_mu_[i_] = ##      ##       # Segment 1: y ~ 1 ##       (x[i_] >= cp_0) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(1)], c(Intercept_1)) * 1 +  ##      ##       # Segment 2: y ~ 1 + (1 | id) ~ 0 + x ##       (x[i_] >= (cp_1 + cp_1_id[id[i_]])) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(2)], c(x_2)) * x_local_2_[i_] ##      ##     # Formula for sigma ##     link_sigma_[i_] = ##      ##       # Segment 1: y ~ 1 ##       (x[i_] >= cp_0) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(3)], c(sigma_1)) * 1 ##  ##     # Likelihood and log-density for family = gaussian() ##     mu_[i_] = link_mu_[i_] ##     sigma_[i_] = max(1e-03, link_sigma_[i_]) ##     y[i_] ~ dnorm(mu_[i_], 1 / sigma_[i_]^2)  # SD as precision ##   } ## }

text: articles mcp website go -depth functionality mcp. executive summary, give quick sense mcp can . mcp models simulating data: * Parameter names Intercept_i (intercepts), cp_i (change points), x_i (slopes), ar*/ma* (autocorrelation), sigma_* (variance). * change point model basically ifelse model. * Generate data supported models using fit$simulate(). See examples , e.g., mcp_examples("demo")$call. Using priors: * See priors fit$prior. * Set priors using mcp(..., prior = list(cp_1 = "dnorm(0, 1)", cp_2 = "dunif(0, 45)"). * default prior change points fast estimation mathematically “messy”. Dirichlet prior (cp_i = "dirichlet(1)") slow beautiful. * Fix parameters specific values using cp_1 = 45. * Share parameters segments using slope_1 = "slope_2". * Truncate priors using T(lower, upper), e.g., Intercept_1 = "dnorm(0, 1) T(0, )". mcp applies automatically change point priors enforce order restriction. true varying change points . * prior predictive checks using mcp(model, data, sample = "prior"). Varying change points: * Get posteriors using ranef(fit). * Plot using plot(fit, facet_by = "my_group") plot_pars(fit, pars = "varying", type = "dens_overlay", ncol = 3). * default priors restrict varying change points lie two adjacent change points. Supported families link functions: * mcp currently supports specific combinations families (gaussian(), binomial(), bernoulli(), poisson(), negbinomial()) link functions (identity, logit, probit, log). * Use informative priors avoid issues using non-default priors. * Use binomial(link = "logit") binomial change points mcp. Also relevant bernoulli(link = "logit"). * Use poisson(link = "log") Poisson change points mcp. * Get results parameter scale rather observed scale using plot(fit, scale = "linear") predict(fit, scale = "linear"). Model comparison hypothesis testing: * Leave-One-Cross-Validation using loo(fit) loo::loo_compare(fit1$loo, fit2$loo). * Compute Savage-Dickey density ratios using hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 = 40"). * Leverage directional conditional tests assess interval hypotheses (hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 > 30 & cp_1 < 50")), combined hypotheses (hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 > 30 & Intercept_1 > Intercept_2")), etc. Modeling variance autoregression: * ~ sigma(1) models intercept change variance. ~ sigma(0 + x) models increasing/decreasing variance. Explicit sigma() formulas use log link, coefficients log-SD scale. * ~ ar(N) models Nth order autoregression residuals. ~ar(N, 0 + x) models increasing/decreasing autocorrelation. * can model anything sigma() ar(). example, ~ x + sigma(1 + x + (x^2)) models polynomial change variance x top slope mean. Get fitted predicted values intervals: * fitted(fit) predict(fit) take many arguments predict -sample --sample values intervals. * Forecasting prior knowledge future change points. Tips, tricks, debugging * Speed fitting using future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3), /fewer iterations, mcp(..., adapt = 500). * Help convergence along using mcp(..., inits = list(cp_1 = 20, Intercept_2 = -3)). * errors caused circularly defined priors.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: mcpfits now work natively posterior tidybayes posterior draw prediction API. Changes include: summary(fit) now reports rank-normalized split-Rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail posterior central quantile intervals instead HDIs. adding as_draws(fit), as_draws_df(fit), tidy_draws(fit), etc. full S3 generic registration posterior tidybayes (spread_draws(), gather_draws()), also soft-deprecates directly accessing fit$mcmc_post. Per-draw methods (summary = FALSE fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik()) now return dot-prefixed columns (.epred, .prediction, .residual, .loglik) tidybayes / ggdist compatibility. nsamples soft-deprecated favor ndraws; which_y deprecated favor dpar. Supports several continuous predictors, categorical predictors, interactions, etc. terms RHS. E.g., ~ 1 + x + x:group + sigma(1 + group) + ar(2, 0 + z). Basically, now “feels” like lm() distributional parameter segment. mcp functions support now, including plot(), fit$simulate(), predict(fit, newdata = ...), hypothesis(), pp_check(), etc. Explore ex = mcp_example("multiple") see action. Default priors generally align brms, adjustments change-point model. Predictor formulas now support group-level effects (sometimes called random varying effects) using familiar lme4 brms syntax. (1 | group) specifies group-level intercept, (1 + x || group) (factor || group) support independent coefficients, including slopes factors. also works inside distributional formulas sigma(1 + (factor || id)). ar(), effect carries later segments redefined disabled (0 | group). See mcp_example("group") worked example. Correlated multi-coefficient | terms yet supported. Use mcp(..., seed = 42) reproducible JAGS sampling. See mcp_example("demo")$call ensure reproducibility across simulation, fit, plotting. mcp_example(...) now shows illustrative plot fitted example default. Disable using plot = FALSE. Prediction methods now accept varying = "cp" varying = "predictor" fast selectors group-level effects corresponding formula part. Exact varying-parameter names remain supported , varying = TRUE selects , ranef() continues return group-level effects. Added deprecation detections, various ways helping users older mcp-versions encounter deprecations. time removed.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Although lot updated, parameter estimates v0.4.0 remain practically identical previous public release (v0.3.4). AR MA intercepts now zero-centered, regularizing dnorm(0, 0.5) T(-1, 1) priors, replacing independent uniform priors. categorical contrasts numeric slopes now use modest normal priors instead heavy-tailed Student-t priors. Coefficients remain direct jointly constrained stationary invertible regions. Gaussian models explicit sigma() formula now model residual standard deviation log link, brms. Models without explicit sigma() unchanged: sigma_1 remains residual SD response-scale half-Student-t prior. Formula transformations now use original predictor values, lm(), glm(), brms. Previously, transformations change-point predictor sin(x) exp(x) restarted segment onset. Bare par_x polynomial bases (par_x^2) remain segment-local support joined segment shapes. Parallel sampling now controlled exclusively active future plan. cores argument mcp() deprecated ignored, remains available backwards compatibility. Use future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3) calling mcp() sample chains parallel, future::plan(future::sequential) shut workers. Without parallel future plan, chains sampled sequentially. Dropped support rel() formulas. ambiguous interaction terms made code hard maintain. Another way achieving functionality via priors may added future versions. Renamed parameters consistent brms: int_i –> Intercept_i; x_1_E2 –> xE2_1; x_1_sin –> sinx_1, etc. arguments fit$simulate() changed accommodate multiple (categorical) predictors. fit$simulate(fit, data, ..., .type = "predict") new argument structure. Note (1) now requires fit first argument, (2) requires data.frame tibble second argument instead just vector par_x, (3) arguments prefixed “.” avoid name conflicts internally mcp. ... model parameters usual. Dropped support mcp(..., data = NULL). now must provide mock-data inform mcp types levels predictor columns. See, e.g., mcp_example("intercepts")$call simple example mcp_example("multiple")$call involved example. docs updated appropriately. Changed arguments order plot(). used arguments first new color_by nice place sequence arguments. plot(fit, lines, geom_data, cp_dens, q_fit, q_predict, ...) plot(fit, q_fit, q_predict, facet_by, color_by, lines, geom_data, ...) Dropped arguments which_y, scale made sense distributional parameters (dpars) several arguments (e.g., q_predict) insensible. Use new plot_dpar() . fit = mcp_example("name") now returns fit directly instead list $fit entry. now defaults sampling model (sample = "post") sample argument now directly passed mcp(..., sample = sample) sample = TRUE deprecated.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Default plot(fit) style updated many ways accommodate multiple regression group-effects. Extended autoregression (ar()) GARMA link-scale residuals Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative-binomial models default links, using ar(..., boundary = 0.1) default keep zero boundary counts finite. Added moving-average terms ma(q), can used alone combined ar(p) segment. Bernoulli models non-default links remain unsupported. Added AR/MA warnings: (1) AR/MA models loo(), predict(), etc. serial dependence currently ignored. Proper handling requires leave-future-blocked cross-validation, currently implemented mcp. (2) posterior probability >10% violation AR-stationarity MA-invertibility. addition (segment-wide) intercepts slopes, now default priors categorical predictors. Memory improvement: mcpfit now < 10% size log-likelihood computed default anymore (fit$mcmc_loglik anymore). can add using fit = add_loglik(fit) (adds fit$loglik) absent, automatically computed calling relevant functions, e.g., loo(fit). Several new arguments loo. loo(fit, pointwise = TRUE) uses loo::loo.function() memory-efficient (slower) computation LOO. new arguments include usual fitted() etc.: loo(fit, ndraws = 1000, arma = FALSE, varying = FALSE). Sampling now 1-10% faster due new formalization underlying JAGS code. plot() now uses filled area change-point densities visually distinguish color-coded fitted lines. Added interpolate_newdata(fit, = NULL) generates data.frame combinations categorical predictors along interpolated continuous predictors. Use include varying-effect groups. documentation shows can useful generating custom plots simple tweaking plot() enough. Added niterations(fit) nchains(fit) convenience. Added log_lik(fit) analogous e.g., fitted(fit). Added prior_summary(fit). compact output shows parameter’s resolved prior bounds; prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) also shows data-dependent rule, plain-language description, source, kind (distribution, alias, expression, constant). Default priors now resolved JAGS code generated, fit$prior generated code longer depend opaque data constants. Added option test hypotheses prior using hypothesis(fit, prior = TRUE). mcp(..., warn = TRUE) now controls runtime convergence warnings (Rhat > 1.01 ESS < 400). Warning also appear summary(fit) footer. introduction multiple regression including categorical predictors (including distributional parameters) come default priors. term involving local par_x, scale multiplied expected segment width “usual”. non-par_x terms, numeric coefficients scaled data model. Briefly, based observed range two values, two standard deviations otherwise, aligning Gelman (2008) prior autoscaling rstanarm.
